"Fake news" has such a Clintony ring to it, doesn't it? It's such an out of touch branding failure. It's a fake insult invented by fake people for fake reasons, and it's meaningless, ridiculous, and... obviously, FAKE! Trump would have done much better.

But because FAKE is such a weak brand, I think those of us who want to can take advantage of that. "Fake news" is full of logical loopholes that we can easily exploit, because "fake" can mean many things, from an outright lie, to a poor copy, to a perfect replica. Fake can even be almost of honorable, if you think about it. To fake an orgasm is to show that you want someone to know you like them, or that you want them to feel good. To fake a smile means you're at least trying. A fake in sports is a legitimate play, and "fake it till you make it" is a powerful trick that might just make you president one day.

But what I think we should target is the assumed connection between fake and news. There are already multiple kinds of "fake news" - from tabloids, to The Onion and all those parody news segments. One instance of "fake" news could be simply news that isn't really news anymore - more commonly known by its other title, "old news." Fake news is already a horribly segmented brand, and this is good for us, because it should be easy to refute.

So we need to attack their label and destroy it, and it really shouldn't be hard.

Let's try to think of it how the brand master would do it. Yes... Trump! Love him or hate him, he knows how to get people thinking about things. Like, me, right now. How does he do it? Let's break it down.

First, he tends to be very visual: Think of "build a wall," or "drain the swamp." Next, he goes immediately for the extreme: Greatest, or Worst. Tremendous, or Sad. Lastly, he doubles down rather than giving up, almost without fail. So, if someone calls Trump a whiner, instead of arguing with them he might say "Yes, I'm a whiner, and I keep whining, and whining, and whining, until I win!" (Yes, he actually said this)

Trump whining to win: http://www.cnn.com/videos/politics/2015/08/11/donald-trump-whining-cuomo-newday.cnn

Sometimes, Trump directly opposes a brand. For example, when people said he was not a conservative. Not being a conservative was actually a really bad image for his brand because it was believable, so he focused some of his genius on refuting this in a clever way, repeatedly.

"Trump is not a conservative": https://youtu.be/26W_CpPaAwc

He mocked the people who said this about him by making a face and repeating their claim in a silly voice. He's done this with other serious arguments as well. The strategy is simple and silly, but effective. If you ever hear something said in a silly voice, it's hard to take it seriously anymore. This is a hypnotic technique used by NLP practitioners and hypnotists. It works especially well for dissipating fears, and you can bet it's being used by the professionals to frame our arguments as ludicrous.

The problem with this argument for us is the stakes are much higher than whether or not someone is a conservative. We can't make the "who the hell cares" argument here because everyone SHOULD care.

I think the best tactic from Trump in a situation similar to what we're going territory now is his "no I'm not, you are" deflection.

"No, you're the puppet": https://youtu.be/UaVWRetR4jg

Again, it's simple and silly, and effective, because it makes the entire debate ridiculous. Yes, it makes him appear petty, but if Hillary continues the attack, it makes her appear even more so.

Since the "fake news" slur is so muddled by the weakness of the FAKE brand, I believe we can simply double down on our most serious claims, ignore the slurs, and throw "fake" right back at them. And be as relentless, factless, and loud as they are. It's the ultimate counter punch.

If nothing else, it will make the fake brand even more meaningless than it already is. But it might also bring down the FAKE MSM with it.
